subject: Memory stabilization hotfix — brief unscheduled maintenance
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lin <sara@nimbusapps.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Memory stabilization hotfix — brief unscheduled maintenance

Hi Sara,

Quick heads-up: over the last hour we observed an increase in memory growth on a small subset of long-running inference sessions serving Nimbus Apps. We've developed a targeted hotfix that reduces the transient KV-cache growth for affected model variants.

We plan a short maintenance window to apply the fix to your production pool at 09:00 PT (approx. 20–30 minutes). Expected customer impact: best-effort zero-downtime; in the worst case we will route affected requests to a compatible fallback model for up to 5 minutes while pods restart.

Actions we're taking:
- Apply hotfix to a single canary instance at 09:00 PT and run 10m smoke tests
- If healthy, roll remaining instances with rolling restarts (no full cluster restart)
- Monitor latency and error rates continuously; automatic rollback if error > 1% over baseline

Attachment: hotfix_readme_v1.md (summary + rollback steps) and kv_cache_stabilization_patch.diff (patch stub).

I know this is short notice — apologies. Will keep you updated in this thread and share a post-action summary after the rollout. Please let me know if there's a strict blackout window we should avoid.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Lin <sara@nimbusapps.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@nimbusapps.com
Date: 2026-09-15T08:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Memory stabilization hotfix — brief unscheduled maintenance

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the quick note.

A couple quick questions from our side:
- Any risk of session state loss for in-progress chat sessions?
- Will embeddings and batch jobs be affected? Our nightly embedding job runs at 02:00 PT; that’s outside your window but want to confirm no carryover config changes.

If fallback routing is used, will responses be clearly labeled? We have a compliance flag we prefer set when model variants change.

Sara Lin
Head of Platform
Nimbus Apps
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lin <sara@nimbusapps.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Memory stabilization hotfix — brief unscheduled maintenance

Sara — short answers:
- Session state: we do not evict user session state. Active sessions will be reattached to restarted worker without losing chat history; transient tokens in RAM may be reloaded from persisted KV when needed.
- Embeddings & batch jobs: not affected by the hotfix; this change targets the small-path memory accounting in model-serving containers, not the embeddings pipeline.
- Fallback labeling: yes — when requests are served by a fallback model we will set the response metadata header x-rdwy-fallback: true and include a one-line note in the tooling response. We'll surface the flag to your engineers via the examples in the attachment.

Planned timeline (updated):
- 09:00 PT — apply patch to canary (single instance)
- 09:10–09:20 PT — smoke tests and latency/err check
- 09:20–09:40 PT — rolling restarts across remaining pool (gradual)
- 09:45 PT — final verification and post-update status

We will not change configuration that would affect your nightly jobs. Patch is code-level memory accounting fix only.

Attachment: included hotfix_readme_v1.md with rollback commands and observability playbook.

Jordan
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T09:31:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Memory stabilization hotfix — brief unscheduled maintenance

Ack — ran a quick smoke on the patch locally and the canary diffs look good (heap delta ~8% lower under the long-session microbenchmark). Will proceed with canary at 09:00. Monica/Evelyn, if production telemetry spikes beyond thresholds, escalate to full rollback per the playbook.

Karthik
Engineering, Runtime
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lin <sara@nimbusapps.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-15T10:43:00-07:00
Subject: Post-update: Memory stabilization hotfix applied to Nimbus Apps (summary)

Sara — quick post-update summary: 

What we did:
- Applied targeted memory-accounting hotfix to your production pool with a staged canary and rolling restart.
- Ran smoke tests and synthetic long-session benchmarks.

Observed outcome:
- Memory growth reduced on observed sessions (median RSS down ~9% across sampled pods).
- No user session state lost; no reported errors from your team during the window.
- Latency remained within baseline ±4% during rollouts.

Artifacts and next steps:
- Hotfix details and rollback commands: hotfix_readme_v1.md (attached).
- Patch diff: kv_cache_stabilization_patch.diff (attached).
- Postmortem draft and follow-up action item doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-hotfix-notes — will add telemetry charts and a longer write-up by EOD.

If you saw anything unexpected on your side please flag it here and we'll investigate ASAP. I'll be creating the final postmortem and scheduling a 30m follow-up review with your platform team tomorrow.

Thanks for the quick coordination and for being flexible on the short notice.

— Jordan
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
